commands.name: encode
commands.about: Encode raw video to a stream.

options.help: Raw 8-bit 4:2:0 frames, back to back; `-` reads stdin.
Plane layout of the input (default i420).
Frame width in pixels (even).
Frame height in pixels (even).
Nominal frame rate: `30`, `29.97` or `30000/1001`.
Number of input frames to code.
Capture time of each frame (mkvmerge timestamp format v2); rate control budgets the real frame intervals.
The input's frames have this size from FRAME on (a key frame with new headers); repeatable.

The stream: IVF for AV1, VP9 and AV2, Annex-B for H.264, HEVC and VVC; `-` writes stdout. A path ending .mp4/.m4v (MP4), .mkv (Matroska) or .webm (VP9, AV1) writes that container, with every coded frame's time (held frames included) and key-frame index (not AV2).
The reconstruction of every coded frame (I420).
One picture per input frame, as a decoder shows it: a frame left uncoded repeats the last one.
The time of every coded frame.
The coded units as RTP packets: pcap for .pcap, otherwise RFC 4571 framing. AV1 carries the Dependency Descriptor (extension id 1), VP9 its layer indices.
Largest RTP packet of --rtp (default 1200).
Dependency Descriptor extension id of --rtp (AV1 default 1, others none).
Output format (`h266` is accepted for vvc). Required.

A rung of the speed ladder; medium is the codec's Default and is used without --preset. A name is a position on that codec's ladder (in this order); not every codec has every rung (`nanocodec params --codec C`); with --scalability L2*/L3* a rung takes the codec's file for that many layers.

Fixed key-frame leaf size (default 16; AV2 8, VVC 32), coded only with the key planner off (`planner.intra_plan` 0; H.264 is always 16): refused where the planner chooses every block size, as the presets do.
Fixed quantiser in the codec's scale (H.264, HEVC: QP 0-51; VVC: QP 0-63; AV1, VP9, AV2: base_q_idx); with --bitrate, the starting quantiser only. One of --qp and --bitrate is required.
Code fixed-QP key frames D quantiser steps finer than --qp (default: the codec chooses). Refused with --bitrate: rate control sizes key frames itself.
Real-time rate control at this target bitrate.
Peak drain rate (default twice the target).
Virtual decoder buffer duration (default 1000 ms).
Decoder buffer fullness when the stream starts, at most the buffer: the first frames may send this much ahead of the drain (x264 --vbv-init, --buf-initial-sz). Default: the whole buffer.
Lowest quantiser rate control may use, in the --qp scale and range.
Highest quantiser rate control may use, in the --qp scale and range.
Largest quantiser change between inter frames (default 4 QP, 20 AV1 indices).
Skip an inter frame that would overflow the buffer even at the highest quantiser.
Never pass one buffer: re-code any frame that would fill it past its capacity (a hard VBV). By default a frame may reach 1.15 buffers, as the reference encoders' worst points do.
Change the target (and peak, buffer) before frame FRAME, as a transport's bandwidth estimate would; repeatable.
A key frame every N frames (default: every 10 seconds of video).
Code input frame FRAME as a key frame, as a receiver's request would; repeatable.

Intra refresh sweep over this many frames in place of periodic key frames (`refresh.period`). With --temporal-layers 2|3 or --scalability LxT2/T3 the layers are fixed and the sweep runs on the base layer. Not with spatial layers, VP9 or AV2. Each sweep's first frame is a recovery point (H.264/HEVC SEI, VVC GDR picture); VVdeC-based players skip the first refresh sweep after a stream start (spec-conformant per H.266 §8.1.1/§8.1.2).
Mark a long-term reference every N frames, for loss recovery (`ltr.interval`).
Hierarchical-P temporal layers; the top layer is droppable. Not with --scalability.
Scalability mode L1T1..L3T3: spatial layers (L2, L3: 2:1 steps) and temporal layers in one stream; `_KEY` codes K-SVC.
Noise handling for a fixed camera over the preset: lowers the bitrate on still noisy scenes; off in every preset.
AV1 only: film grain synthesis, STRENGTH relative to the measured source noise.
Colour description to signal (ISO/IEC 23091-2 code points for P,T,M).
Sample range to signal.
Header timing information (default nominal; variable with --timestamps); constant also codes every frame (no frame holds). VP9 and AV2 streams carry no timing, so they refuse variable.
A parameter file (one `name = value` per line, `#` comments), over the preset.
One parameter, over the file; repeatable. `nanocodec params` lists them.
With --bitrate: one CSV row per frame of rate control's state.
Per-plane squared error of every shown picture against --sse-reference (CSV).
The reference frames for --sse-log.
CSV of each layer picture's size, bytes and MD5.

JSON of the frame-level filter searches' units by outcome (off, unchanged), by tool and frame role; "given": [units, off, unchanged] of the searched units by their own last outcomes (off at the last 1, 2, 4 searches, on, unchanged) and content (quiet: mostly coded without residual).

Decision labels for learned models: per superblock its inputs and coded cost, per searched node every candidate's coded cost and time, as .npy columns (docs/analysis/nn-dataset-schema.md). The stream is unchanged; encoding is slower.

With --label-dump: also code every superblock with these parameters on top of the preset's, the rest of the frame as the preset codes it, recording its J and time (sb/tool_cost, sb/tool_ns); repeatable. Engine decision./planner. parameters, or the codec's per-superblock ones.
JSON summary of per-layer bytes, rates and references.
With --bitrate: impose these quantisers on rate control's plan, by frame.
QP offsets per 8x8 luma cell imposed on key frames, by input frame (an oracle: `frame N`, then one line of offsets per cell row).
Every inter superblock's coded partition (an oracle: the transplant log).
Code a --partition-record log's partitions in place of the plan, without the RD partition search (an oracle: the partition transplant).
Every frame's analysis per 8x8 luma cell (binary: variance, motion SAD and vector).
Report frame FRAME (or spatial layer LAYER of it) lost; every other frame is acknowledged.

commands.name: decode
commands.about: Decode a stream, ours or another encoder's, within the supported profiles (gaps: docs/FAQ.md#conformance).

options.help: Stream format. Required.
The stream (IVF or Annex-B); `-` reads stdin.
Decoded frames as raw I420 (16-bit little-endian above 8 bits); `-` writes stdout.
One MD5 line per shown frame.
1: decode every frame and write nothing (for timing).
Time N in-process decodes of the stream in memory (JSON lines).
AV1: 0 shows frames without film grain.
AV1 or VP9 operating point to decode.
AV1 or VP9: 1 writes every spatial layer's picture.
AV1: 1 decodes frames beyond the level 6.3 size bound (conformance streams).
AV1: 0 writes monochrome pictures as luma only (aomdec --rawvideo, dav1d).

commands.name: extract
commands.about: Keep a temporal or spatial sub-stream of a stream, without re-encoding.

options.help: Stream format. Required.
The stream.
The kept sub-stream.
Temporal layers the stream was coded with.
Keep temporal layers 0..M (below --temporal-layers).
List each access unit's temporal layer instead of extracting.
AV1 or VP9: keep the spatial base layer.
AV1 or VP9: keep this operating point.
VP9: the encoder's layer sidecar to split by.

commands.name: packetize
commands.about: A stream file (IVF or Annex B) to RTP packets (no Dependency Descriptor: use encode --rtp).

options.help: Stream format (not av2). Required.
The stream.
pcap for .pcap, otherwise RFC 4571 framing.
Largest RTP packet (default 1200).
RTP payload type (default 96).
Annex-B input: frames per second for timestamps (default 30).
VP9 payload descriptor mode (default flexible).

commands.name: depacketize
commands.about: RTP packets (pcap or RFC 4571) to a stream file, through the receiver's loss handling.

options.help: Stream format (not av2). Required.
The capture.
IVF (AV1, VP9) or Annex B.
Keep only this payload type.
Dependency Descriptor extension id (AV1 default 1, others none).
Forward only spatial layers 0..S and temporal layers 0..T first, by the Dependency Descriptor (VP9 without one: its payload descriptor), as a forwarding server would.
VP9 --layers: upper layers predict from the layer below on every picture (full, default) or on key pictures only (key: K-SVC).
With --layers: also write the forwarded packets (pcap for .pcap, otherwise RFC 4571).
Keep delivering after a loss instead of waiting for a key frame.

commands.name: session
commands.about: Encoder and receiver stepped by commands on stdin (encode options, no --output).

options.help: One picture per input frame: what the viewer saw.
Decode only frames whose listed references arrived (transport, the default), or every arrived frame.
AV1 operating point the receiver decodes.

commands.name: params
commands.about: List every tunable parameter with its default and range, and the presets.

options.help: Show this codec's defaults and presets.

commands.name: stat
commands.about: Coding-tool statistics of a stream (analysis builds: --features analysis).

options.help: Stream format.
The stream.
Write the statistics as JSON.
HEVC, H.264: also write every picture's block records (packed, little-endian).
